findings.title: Bare list/dict annotations in new service modules
findings.problem: code-quality.md (Types And Imports) asks for parameterized generics and spelled-out types for duck-typed params in new modules. get_masked_prompt_variables(prompt_variables: list) -> list (sensitive_prompt_variables.py:89) and, in inline_credentials.py, validate_assistant_inline_integrations(...) -> dict (:27), _check_toolkit_credentials(toolkits) -> list (:52), _check_object_credential_values(obj, credential_type, **kwargs) -> list (:82), _check_mcp_server_credentials(mcp_servers) -> list (:113) and _build_validation_result(inline_credentials) -> dict (:169) use bare list/dict or leave params unannotated. The signatures were carried over from the old router code, but they now live in new modules and ruff selects no ANN/UP rule, so no gate catches it.
findings.impact: Documented standard unmet on a newly public service surface (functions renamed from underscore-private); callers and type checkers get no element types. The fix is annotation-only: both modules use `from __future__ import annotations`, so it has no runtime effect and leaves bodies, behaviour and the OpenAPI baselines untouched.
findings.recommendation: Annotate signatures only, leaving bodies and docstrings unchanged (AC2 body check): get_masked_prompt_variables(prompt_variables: list[PromptVariable | dict[str, object]]) -> list[dict[str, object]]; validate_assistant_inline_integrations(...) -> dict[str, object]; _build_validation_result(inline_credentials: list[InlineCredential]) -> dict[str, object]; _check_toolkit_credentials and _check_mcp_server_credentials take the list of the model type the caller passes (assistant.toolkits, assistant.mcp_servers) and return list[InlineCredential]; _check_object_credential_values(obj: object, credential_type: str, **kwargs: object) -> list[InlineCredential]. Import the model types under TYPE_CHECKING.
